::: {#case .lx-sec}
```{=html}
<div class="lx-case">
<div class="lx-case-part"><p class="lx-eyebrow">1 · The puzzle</p><p>In <span class="lx-term" data-term="ercot">ERCOT</span>, wind and solar output is concentrated far from electricity demand in the north and southeast, and from hydrogen demand on the Gulf Coast.</p>
<p>How much planned renewable capacity is built by 2030, and how fast demand grows, are both uncertain.</p></div>
<div class="lx-case-part"><p class="lx-eyebrow">2 · The question in one sentence</p><p class="lx-case-q">Where should <span class="lx-term" data-term="electrolyzer">electrolyzers</span>, hydrogen storage and <span class="lx-term" data-term="fuel-cell">fuel cells</span> be built in ERCOT, and how should hydrogen move between zones, to absorb surplus renewable generation and supply industrial hydrogen demand under uncertain 2030 renewable build-out?</p><p class="lx-hint">Question type: prescriptive (what should be built, where, and how should it run?).</p></div>
<div class="lx-case-part"><p class="lx-eyebrow">3 · Scale and boundary</p><ul><li><b>Inside:</b> ERCOT's eight weather zones, every hour of a year (8,760 hours), nine scenarios of renewable build-out and electricity demand, and industrial hydrogen demand in each zone.</li><li><b>Left out:</b> uncertainty in hydrogen demand, which is held fixed; truck and rail transport; post-2023 federal hydrogen credit rules.</li></ul></div>
<div class="lx-case-part"><p class="lx-eyebrow">4 · Decisions, goal and rules, in words</p><ul><li><b>Decisions:</b> the sizes of electrolyzers, hydrogen tanks and fuel cells in each zone, chosen once; then, in each scenario, how batteries, electrolysis, fuel cells, gas-fired backup, <span class="lx-term" data-term="gas-reformer">reformer hydrogen</span> and pipeline flows run every hour.</li><li><b>Goal:</b> the lowest <span class="lx-term" data-term="expected-value">expected cost</span> over all nine scenarios, net of hydrogen and oxygen sales, with the CO₂ from gas plants and reformers captured and stored at a cost.</li><li><b>Rules:</b> electricity demand is met in every zone and hour; industrial hydrogen demand is met by green or reformer hydrogen; hydrogen moves only by pipeline between neighbouring zones; no unit runs above its size.</li></ul></div>
<div class="lx-case-part wide"><p class="lx-eyebrow">5 · Data and method</p><p class="lx-hint">The method in general: choose equipment sizes now, then run them differently in each possible future, weighing each future's cost by its chance.</p><ul><li>Inputs are built from ERCOT's 60-day market disclosures, the <span class="lx-term" data-term="lbnl">LBNL</span> <span class="lx-term" data-term="interconnection-queue">interconnection queue</span> and <span class="lx-term" data-term="eia">EIA</span> data.</li><li>The same hourly <span class="lx-term" data-term="capacity-factor">capacity factors</span> of each zone scale existing and planned wind and solar, so both share one hourly basis.</li><li>A <span class="lx-term" data-term="two-stage-stochastic-program">two-stage stochastic linear program</span> sized electrolyzers, hydrogen tanks and fuel cells once in each of ERCOT's eight weather zones, with hydrogen pipelines between neighbouring zones, then scheduled the system hour by hour over a full year in nine scenarios: <ul><li>three completion rates of planned renewable capacity by three electricity-demand levels.</li></ul></li><li>Hydrogen equipment is sized once, then operated hour by hour in nine scenarios; the sizes minimize expected cost over all nine scenarios instead of fitting a single forecast.</li></ul></div>
<div class="lx-case-part wide"><p class="lx-eyebrow">6 · What came out, and where it holds</p>
<blockquote class="lx-excerpt" data-source="excerpt:txh2"><p>When gas-fired backup power became much more expensive, the model built fuel cells and turned stored green hydrogen back into electricity.</p><p>Industry then drew more hydrogen from gas reformers, and the round trip from power to hydrogen and back lost energy, so total emissions rose although gas-plant emissions fell.</p><p>Electrolyzers and hydrogen tanks, combined with hydrogen transport between zones, could meet most of the hydrogen demand in certain zones.</p><p>Across ERCOT, renewable (green) hydrogen covered only a few percent of industrial hydrogen demand; reformer hydrogen remained the main supply.</p><footer>From: Li et al. (2025), <a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijhydene.2025.02.303">International Journal of Hydrogen Energy</a>.</footer></blockquote>
<p class="lx-hint">Inputs reflect 2022–2023 conditions; post-2023 federal hydrogen credit rules are not modeled.</p>
<p class="lx-hint">Holds when: ERCOT's eight weather zones, inputs from 2022–2023, and hydrogen demand held fixed; the emissions result comes from runs in which power from gas-fired plants became more expensive.</p>
<p class="lx-hint">Leaves out: post-2023 federal hydrogen credit rules; truck and rail transport.</p></div>
</div>
<div class="lx-interactive" data-learn="cf3" data-src="../assets/learn/data/cf3-hydrogen-under-uncertainty.json ../assets/learn/data/f01-five-scales.json">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">The study in time</p>
```

## The idea behind it, then where the result holds
:::

```{=html}
<div class="lx-interactive" data-learn="cf3-idea" data-src="../assets/learn/data/cf3-hydrogen-under-uncertainty.json ../assets/learn/data/m08-stochastic-robust.json">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<!-- cf3-idea:start (written from the toy model by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Size it before the wind is built (illustrative)</p><p class="lx-hint">M8's toy: one windy zone, three build-outs with chances 25%, 50% and 25%, illustrative round numbers in 2025 dollars.</p><ul class="lx-hint cf3-defs"><li><b>Plan for the average:</b> the best size if the wind built were sure to equal its average, 5,000 MW.</li><li><b>Hedged plan:</b> the size with the lowest <span class="lx-term" data-term="expected-value">expected cost</span>, each build-out's cost weighted by its chance.</li><li><b>Worst-case plan:</b> the size whose cost in the worst build-out is lowest; it uses no chances.</li></ul><div class="lx-scroll-x"><table class="lx-mini-table cf3-res"><caption class="lx-hint">Annual cost of the hydrogen supply for three sizes, in each build-out and in expectation</caption><thead><tr><th scope="col">Plan</th><th scope="col">Size</th><th scope="col">None built (25%)</th><th scope="col">Half built (50%)</th><th scope="col">All built (25%)</th><th scope="col">Expected</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">Plan for the average</th><td class="n">1,300 MW</td><td class="n">$767.89M</td><td class="n">$662.63M</td><td class="n">$601.72M</td><td class="n">$673.72M</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Hedged plan</th><td class="n">845 MW</td><td class="n">$731.49M</td><td class="n">$663.09M</td><td class="n">$626.74M</td><td class="n">$671.10M</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Worst-case plan</th><td class="n">380 MW</td><td class="n">$703.40M</td><td class="n">$688.66M</td><td class="n">$652.32M</td><td class="n">$683.26M</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="cf3-worked">Expected cost of the hedged plan: 25% × $731.49M + 50% × $663.09M + 25% × $626.74M = $671.10M a year.</p><p class="lx-hint">A chance-weighted average: not a guaranteed cost, and not what any one build-out costs.</p><p class="lx-hint">With gas reformers alone, every build-out costs $709.56M a year.</p><details class="lx-textalt"><summary>The toy's assumptions and its wind blocks</summary><ul><li>Illustrative: the zone's lines and local demand take up to 1,000 MW of wind in any hour; wind above that is surplus, curtailed unless an electrolyzer uses it.</li><li>Illustrative: 3,000 MW of wind built, 4,000 MW more planned; how much of the planned wind gets built is the uncertainty.</li><li>Illustrative: $80,000 per MW a year, the annualized capital and fixed upkeep; 18 kg of hydrogen per MWh (about 55 kWh per kg). It runs only on surplus wind.</li><li>Illustrative: industry takes 54,000 kg of hydrogen every hour; what the electrolyzer does not make comes from gas reformers at $1.50 per kg.</li><li>Surplus wind is free: the electrolyzer pays only its own yearly cost, and wind it does not use is <span class="lx-term" data-term="curtailment">curtailed</span>.</li><li>The year is five blocks of hours sorted by wind output (a <span class="lx-term" data-term="duration-curve">duration curve</span>), not 8,760 hours in time order.</li><li>Industry's hydrogen demand is steady: the same in every hour and every build-out.</li><li>One zone: no hydrogen storage, no fuel cells and no pipelines; reformer hydrogen has one fixed price.</li></ul><div class="lx-scroll-x"><table class="lx-mini-table"><caption class="lx-hint">The five wind blocks: SPP's 2025 hourly wind shape scaled to 33.8%, sorted and cut</caption><thead><tr><th scope="col">Wind block</th><th scope="col">Hours a year</th><th scope="col">Capacity factor</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">Windiest 500 hours</th><td class="n">500</td><td class="n">57.1%</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Next 1,000 hours</th><td class="n">1,000</td><td class="n">51.7%</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Next 1,500 hours</th><td class="n">1,500</td><td class="n">46%</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Next 2,000 hours</th><td class="n">2,000</td><td class="n">36.9%</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Calmest 3,760 hours</th><td class="n">3,760</td><td class="n">19.4%</td></tr></tbody></table></div></details>
<!-- cf3-idea:end -->
</div>
</div>
<div class="lx-xcard">
<header class="lx-x-head"><h3>Slide the price of gas-fired power</h3></header>
<div class="explainer" data-explainer="txh2">
<ol class="ex-fallback lx-ex-static"><li>When gas-fired backup power becomes more expensive, the model starts to use stored green hydrogen in fuel cells to make electricity in hours of low wind and sun.</li><li>That hydrogen no longer supplies industry, so gas reformers fill the gap with fossil hydrogen.</li><li>Converting electricity to hydrogen and back loses energy, so in the paper's high-price cases total emissions rose even though emissions from gas plants fell.</li></ol>
</div>
<p class="lx-hint">Illustrative model with stylized numbers: it shows the mechanism described in the paper, not the study's data or results.</p>
</div>
<div id="cf3-explain" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<!-- cf3-bound:start (written from the data file by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Where the result holds</p><dl class="lx-ideas"><dt>It holds when</dt><dd><ul><li><span class="lx-term" data-term="ercot">ERCOT</span>'s eight weather zones, every hour of one year, in nine scenarios of renewable build-out and electricity demand;</li><li>inputs reflect 2022–2023 conditions;</li><li>hydrogen demand is held fixed across scenarios;</li><li>the CO₂ from gas plants and reformers is captured and stored at a cost;</li><li>the emissions result comes from sensitivity runs in which power from gas-fired plants became more expensive.</li></ul></dd><dt>It leaves out</dt><dd><ul><li>post-2023 federal hydrogen credit rules;</li><li>uncertainty in hydrogen demand;</li><li>truck and rail transport of hydrogen.</li></ul></dd></dl><p class="lx-hint">From Li et al. (2025), International Journal of Hydrogen Energy.</p>
<!-- cf3-bound:end -->
</div>
</div>

<script src="../assets/explainers/txh2.js" defer></script>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>Sizes now, operation later, in one program</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- Sizes chosen before the uncertainty resolves are [here-and-now]{.lx-term term="here-and-now"} decisions; how the equipment runs in each scenario is [recourse]{.lx-term term="recourse"}.
- One [linear program]{.lx-term term="linear-program"} holds both: one size, one copy of the operation for each scenario, each copy's cost weighted by its chance.
- [M8](m08-stochastic-robust.html) builds a small one in the browser, prices the plan for the average future against it, and compares robust plans that use no chances.

## Check yourself, then try it
:::

```{=html}
<div class="lx-myths" data-quiz="cf3-myth">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="likely" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “The plan for the most likely future is the best plan to build now.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. In the toy, the plan for the middle build-out (1,300 MW) is expected to cost $2.62M a year more than the hedged plan (845 MW), which weighs all three.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="hedge" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “A hedged plan beats building nothing in every build-out.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. In the toy, if none of the planned wind is built, the hedged plan costs $731.49M a year against $709.56M with gas reformers alone. It wins on average, not in every branch.</p></details>
</div>
</div>
<div class="lx-card lx-case-try">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">With open code</p>
<p class="lx-hint">Optional, about 30 minutes; needs Python 3.10 or later (<a href="b02-python-data.html">lesson B2</a>).</p>
<p>Try it yourself: the framework solves a small invented region (four zones, three days) in a few seconds.</p>
<p>Halve the capital cost of the hydrogen equipment, or allow ±5% load flexibility, and compare the sizes and the emissions.</p>
<p>Its numbers say nothing about ERCOT or Texas.</p>
<p><a href="https://github.com/Henryutd2021/txh2-ercot-hydrogen">txh2-ercot-hydrogen</a>: public example repository · MIT licence · synthetic data.</p>
</div>
```
